sermons.title: Joy Broke Thru
sermons.description: Have you ever hesitated to act on God's calling, only to miss out on a divine opportunity? In a powerful message, Pastor Jacob explores Mary's immediate response to God's extraordinary plan through the lens of faith in action. Drawing from Luke's gospel, he illuminates how Mary, upon learning she would bear the Son of God, didn't wait for additional signs but acted promptly by visiting Elizabeth – a journey that validated her faith through Elizabeth's Spirit-filled confirmation. Pastor Jacob weaves this biblical narrative with personal testimonies, including his family's leap of faith in moving to Vietnam with minimal support, demonstrating how God's affirmation often follows, rather than precedes, our steps of obedience. He beautifully connects Mary's story to God's ongoing "stream of mercy" flowing from generation to generation, from Abraham to the present day, even manifesting in modern-day Vietnam where thousands gather to hear the Gospel. The message culminates in an urgent invitation to step into this divine flow, whether through first-time faith in Christ or renewed commitment to God's specific calling, emphasizing that joy breaks through when "faith goes, God shows, and praise flows."
sermons.speaker: Jacob Bloemberg

sermons.title: Peace Broke Thru
sermons.description: Have you ever wondered how a moment of peace could emerge from the depths of war? In Kester's powerful message, he transported us back to the remarkable Christmas truce of 1914, where enemies laid down their weapons to celebrate Christ's birth. Through this poignant historical lens, he illuminated how true peace broke through in an even more extraordinary way – through God's choice to send His Son through Mary, a humble girl from obscure Nazareth. Drawing from Luke's account of the Annunciation, Pastor Kester revealed how the eternal Son of God chose to become dependent on a human mother, demonstrating that genuine peace comes through humility, not human pride or power. Mary's remarkable response of faithful surrender, despite facing potential shame and uncertainty, shows us that lasting peace comes through trusting God's promises and purposes. The message challenges us to consider: Will we, like Mary, embrace God's seemingly impossible plan, allowing His peace to break through the conflicts in our own hearts and lives? As we approach Christmas, we're called to remember that true peace isn't found in human efforts, but in submitting to the humble King who chose to enter our broken world.
sermons.speaker: Kester Scandrett

sermons.title: Hope Broke Thru
sermons.description: What does it mean to trust in a world filled with fake news and artificial realities? Pastor Jacob tackles this timely question through the lens of the first Christmas story, particularly focusing on Zechariah's encounter with the angel Gabriel. Drawing from Luke's meticulously researched account, he illuminates how God broke 400 years of seeming silence with an extraordinary announcement in the temple. Through Zechariah and Elizabeth's story - a faithful couple bearing the pain of childlessness well into their senior years - Pastor Jacob reveals how God's plans unfold in perfect timing, even when hope seems lost. He masterfully connects their struggle to trust God's seemingly impossible promise with our modern skepticism about the Christmas story itself. The sermon challenges listeners to move beyond mere doubt to decisive response, emphasizing that God doesn't require ability but availability. As we enter the Advent season, Pastor Jacob calls the congregation to embrace the historical reliability of the Christmas narrative and, more importantly, to say "yes" to participating in God's ongoing mission of reconciliation and restoration through Christ.
sermons.speaker: Jacob Bloemberg
